title: French Verb ALLER - to go. Learn ALL the Tenses Fast
meta_description: French verb ALLER is a top ten French verb. Learn ALL the tenses here in ONE SHOT using the colour-coded verb tables. Aller can be used as an easy way to express the future tense.
h1: French Verb ALLER - to go
subtitle: A Top Ten French Verb
mnemonic: Imagine you GO down the ALLEY to ALLAY his fears.
intro_html:
MORE on the FRENCH VERB ALLER The first meaning of the French verb aller is to go: Òu vas-tu? Je vais á la boulangerie. Where are you going? I’m going to the bakery. It can also be used to ask about people’s health: Comment vas-tu ? Je vais bien merci. How are you? I’m fine thank you. Comment va ta jambe ? Elle me fait encore un peu mal. How is your leg? It still hurts a little. Here are some other expressions using the French verb aller : Cette robe te va comme un gant. This dress fits you like a glove. Faire des va-et-vient to go back and forth Va-t’en! Get away! Allez-y! Go ahead! Allez, prends-le! Come on, take it! Les verres vont au-dessus de l’évier. Glasses go above the sink. Allez les Bleus! Come on France! Go France! Les Bleus signifies the blue jerseys of the French national football and rugby teams. Aller is also used as a 'future' tense, in the same way as we use the expression 'going to' in English: Je vais étudier à la Sorbonne. I am going to study at the Sorbonne (University in Paris). Il va venir tout de suite. He is going to come soon. On va voir. We will see. (One will see).

title: French Verb DEVOIR - must, to have to in French
meta_description: French verb DEVOIR is one of the top ten French verbs. Learn all the tenses and conjugations with our video and our colour-coded verb tables.
h1: French Verb DEVOIR: to have to, must in French
subtitle: 5 Fun Facts on DEVOIR
mnemonic: Imagine that to kill a DEVIL you MUST DEVOUR it.
intro_html:
MORE on the FRENCH VERB devoir The French verb devoir means to have to: Je dois finir ce livre. I have to finish that book. Tu dois faire plus attention à tes affaires. You must pay more attention/take more care of your things/affairs. It can also be translated as must: Tu es rentré tard hier soir, tu dois être fatigué. You came home late last night, you must be tired. Elles doivent finir leurs devoirs avant de sortir. They must finish their homeworks before they go out. The French verb devoir can also mean: Tu me dois 50€. You owe me 50€. Je te dois une fière chandelle ! I am deeply indebted to you! Une femme se doit d’être présentable. A lady has to be presentable.

meta_description: French verb ETRE means 'to be'. The fastest way to learn ALL the tenses is with our colour-coded VERB TABLE - past, present and future
h1: French Verb ETRE - être (to be)
mnemonic: Imagine Shakespeare says, "to be or not to be is an ATTRA ctive thought!
intro_html:
MORE on the FRENCH VERB être Je suis en France: I am in France. Il est Français: He is French. La France est en Europe: France is in Europe. Elle était contente: She was happy.

Je suis en France: I am in France. Il est Français: He is French. La France est en Europe: France is in Europe. Elle était contente: She was happy.

Je suis en France: I am in France.

Il est Français: He is French.

La France est en Europe: France is in Europe.

Elle était contente: She was happy.
notes_html: HOW TO CONQUER the CONJUGATION of ÊTRE The French verb for be être is an auxiliary . An auxiliary verb is one that is used to build other tenses like the compound tenses. These are phrases like: I had come: je suis venu (or je suis venue for a female talking) we had gone: nous sommes allés ), and such like. Learn to conjugate être . French Verbs List . Repeating these tables aloud 10 times throughout the day will better embed the patterns into your subconscious, and your long term memory. Reciting aloud is a great way for you to practice your pronunciation, and helps you to memorize the conjugations.

title: French Verb lower-baisser Verb Table
meta_description: French verb lower-baisser and its synonym abaisser are useful ER verbs. Check out the memory trigger to help you remember this word. Verb Table conjugated.
h1: French Verb lower: baisser (also to reduce, bring down ...)
mnemonic: Imagine you lower a BASS guitar!
intro_html: MORE on the FRENCH VERBS baisser et abaisser The two words on baisser et abaisser are very similar in use. The difference between the two is subtle, and you will be completely UNDERSTOOD if you use the two interchangeably. However abaisser would (generally) suggest something more 'long lasting'. Les magasins ont abaissé les prix de cette marque. The stores have dropped the price of that brand. (It is unlikely that they will rise). Les magasins ont baissé les prix de cette marque. The stores have dropped the price of that brand. (It suggests that it could be a short term thing, that they will rise again later). baisser le drapeau: lower the flag; baisser le volume: lower the volume; baisser les prix: drop prices; baisser le taux de chômage: lower the unemployment rate; baisser le taux de croissance: lower the growth rate; baisser le niveau de productivité: lower the level of productivity; baisser la garde: drop one's guard; faire baisser: to cause to lower something; faire baisser les yeux: to stare; baisser les yeux: to lower one's eyes; baisser la tête: lower one's head; to duck the head; to hang one's head e.g. in shame, in sorrow; baisser les bras: to drop one's arms; which colloquially means to cave in, to yield, to give up; s'abaisser: to demean oneself. s'abaisser: to lower oneself - for example to lower oneself slowly into the bathtub, or into a swimming pool. To carefully lower yourself into a manhole for example.
notes_html: HOW TO CONQUER FRENCH VERB CONJUGATION The French verb for lower, baisser is another regular ER verb conjugated using the same pattern of endings as 5,000+ other regular ER verbs. Learn to conjugate baisser and it will reinforce the pattern for ALL regular ER verbs, these being the most common French verbs. Do a series of ER verbs every day for a month and you will have a solid knowledge of the ER verbs' conjugation patterns. Keep doing them with a new one every day from the French Verbs List . Repeating these tables aloud 10 times throughout the day will better embed the patterns into your subconscious, and your long term memory. Reciting aloud is a great way for you to practice your pronunciation, and helps you to memorize the conjugations.

la chaise à basculer : rocking chair le cheval à basculer : rocking horse faire basculer: to tip up, to cause something or someone to tip off-balance faire la bascule: to rock, to see-saw la balance à bascule: scales for weighing basculant: something that rocks, tilts, topples une caisse basculante: a tip-tray (on a tip-truck)
notes_html: HOW TO CONQUER FRENCH VERB CONJUGATION The French verb for tilt, basculer is another regular ER verb conjugated using the same pattern of endings as 5,000+ other regular ER verbs. Learn to conjugate basculer and it will reinforce the pattern for ALL regular ER verbs, these being the most common French verbs. Do a series of ER verbs every day for a month and you will have a solid knowledge of the ER verbs' conjugation patterns. Keep doing them with a new one every day from the French Verbs List . Repeating these tables aloud 10 times throughout the day will better embed the patterns into your subconscious, and your long term memory. Reciting aloud is a great way for you to practice your pronunciation, and helps you to memorize the conjugations.

subtitle: Just add an Infinitive + 5 Things to Know about VOULOIR
mnemonic: Imagine that during the WOOL WAR they WANTED wool.
intro_html:
MORE on the FRENCH VERB vouloir WANT in FRENCH is VOULOIR The French verb vouloir means to want: Je ne veux pas de ton aide. I don’t want your help. Je voulais juste te dire que je suis désolée. I just wanted to say I’m sorry. Elle lui en veut de lui avoir dit qu’elle était grosse. She’s mad at him for calling her fat. You saw above the verb table how any verb infinitive can be put after a vouloir phrase to make a useful phrase. You can also put a noun after such a vouloir phrase to show that you want a particular thing. Je veux l'orange. I want the orange. Patrique voudrais la pomme. Patrique would like the apple. Nous voudrions le vin blanc. We would like the white wine. Tu veux le rouge ou le noir? Do you want the red one or the black one? Comme tu veux. As you wish. Veuillez patienter, un de nos agents va répondre à votre appel. Please be patient, one of our agents is going to answer your call. Tu vois ce que je veux dire. You know what I mean. Tu sais où sont mes chaussures ? Do you know where my shoes are? Comment veux-tu que je le sache, ce n’est pas moi qui les porte. How should I know? It's not me that wears them.

intro_html:
MORE on the SPANISH VERB apretar apretar can also mean: to squeeze, to grip, to clutch; to press or pull; to intensify, to get worse. apretarse (vr): to huddle together, to squeeze together. apretar a hacer algo: to begin to do something. apretar a correr: to break into a run. apretar la mano a alguien: to shake someone's hand. apretar bien: to clench. apretar el puño: to clench one's fist. ¡Aprieta! Nonsense! Good grief! apretar a alguien: to put pressure on someone. apretar el cinturón: to tighten the belt. apretar el acelerador: to put one's foot down on the accelerator. apretar los tornillos: to tighten the screws. vos replaces tú - you, informal, singular - - in Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay and also in some countries of Central America. Sometimes it also replaces the formal singular 'Usted'. In irregular AR verbs, the conjugations remain the same as for tú except for the addition of accents in the following tenses: Presente: vos apretás Imperativo: ¡apretá! intro_html:
MORE on the SPANISH VERB volar volar can also mean: to blow up; to swipe, to nick (coll:Mex,Ven). volarse (vr): to fly something /someone. volando (pres.part/adj) flying/ in a rush. irse volando: to rush/hurry off (lit. to fly off). el vuelo (nm): flight. tomar vuelo: to take flight. horas de vuelo: flight time. alzar/levantar el vuelo: to fly away / off. El tiempo vuela: Time flies. mandar a volar (a alguien): to tell someone to get lost. tener miedo a volar: to have a fear of flying. volar por las escaleras: to fly down the stairs. vos replaces tú - you, informal, singular - - in Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay and also in some countries of Central America. Sometimes it also replaces the formal singular 'Usted'. In irregular AR verbs, the conjugations remain the same as for tú except for the addition of accents in the following tenses: Presente: vos volás Imperativo: ¡volá!
